title: Introduce graded egress dampener and proactive rejoin guard (hotfix)
author: Leah Park
description: Context: Recent incident (SUP-7890) exposed a pathological interaction between regional KV-drain timing and our egress throttles that caused aggressive connection reopens during transient egress pressure, amplifying downstream latency spikes. This PR introduces a graded egress dampener to smooth egress capacity reductions and a proactive rejoin guard to reduce stormy connection re-establishes. Summary of changes: 1) egress/dampener: new graded dampener module that applies a token-bucket backed smoothing window on egress reductions, with decaying step sizes per-tenant so sudden egress caps are ramped over a configurable window (default 30s). 2) recon/probe: proactive rejoin guard that tracks last-closed-epoch per connection and enforces a jittered exponential backoff with a lightweight health probe before allowing full-weighted rejoin; ties into existing lease metadata (prevents churning when upstream regional probes are noisy). 3) telemetry: added telemetry hooks and SLI emitters (egress_dampener_effect, rejoin_backoff_count, rejoin_probe_latency_p50/p95) and an SLO inspection alert rule that surfaces rapid tenant rejoin churn. 4) safety: feature-gated behind runtime flag runtime.features.graded_egress_dampener; default enabled only in regions with high egress variance. Motivation: Smooth, predictable degradation preserves SLOs for high-value tenants by avoiding oscillatory reopen-and-evict cycles that lead to KV mis-synchronization and cascading failovers. Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-4215) - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] local chaos testing with synthetic egress spike harness - [x] telemetry & dashboards updated - [x] canary rollout plan attached Testing performed: unit tests for dampener thresholds and backoff logic; integration runs in perf-lab with staged egress caps verifying 70-90% reduction in rejoin churn; end-to-end smoke in canary region us-west2 for 6 hours with no regression in latency P95 and controlled increases in tail when egress intentionally reduced Rollout plan: 1) Deploy feature-gate off to main rollout across regions 2) Enable in canary region (us-west2) for 24h, monitor egress_dampener_effect and rejoin_backoff_count 3) Gradually enable in other regions with 10% traffic ramp every 2h 4) After 72h stable, flip default to enabled for all regions Rollback plan: flip runtime.features.graded_egress_dampener=false which immediately disables dampener and restores previous egress behavior; rejoin guards have a fast-fail safety mode when disabled Observability notes: - New dashboard: Reliability / Egress Dampener (panels for effect size, per-tenant smoothing, probe success) - Added SLO alert rule: SLO-REJOIN-CHURN (fires on >5% tenants with >3 rejoins/min sustained for 10m) Security & compliance: no changes to data plane or persisted PII. KMS/HSM not touched. Related: references SUP-7890, ENG-4215 and includes follow-up work item to tune tenant decay constants (ENG-4301).

ci_checks: integration-tests: flaky (1 failure on rejoin_probe_timeout, rerun passed)
release_notes: Hotfix: Smooth egress reductions with new graded dampener; reduce rejoin storming via proactive backoff/probe guard. Improves regional failover stability and reduces tenant churn during transient egress pressure.
testing_summary: Unit + integration tests added. Perf-lab synthetic egress spike showed 70-90% reduction in rejoin events; canary run in us-west2 for 6h with no regression to request P95. One flaky integration test observed and fixed in CI.
rollout_plan: Feature-gated rollout: off by default; enable in canary (us-west2) -> incremental region ramps -> full enable after 72h stable. Quick rollback via feature flag.
rollback_plan: Toggle runtime.features.graded_egress_dampener=false to disable dampener immediately; rejoin guard is safe-disabled and connections revert to previous reopen policy.
notes: Follow-up: tune per-tenant decay constants (ENG-4301), add historical SLO backfill to compare pre/post dampener impact, and evaluate using dampener for planned maintenance windows.
